whoTheyAre.summary: The live source identifies Aizo in Benin and ties the record to Gbe, Ayizo (ayb). Glottolog independently identifies Ayizo Gbe in Benin, while SIL's Gbe-family survey emphasizes that the relationships among Gbe varieties form a chain that should not be forced into an overly simple dialect-versus-language classification.

religionAndCommunity.summary: PeopleGroups.org supplies an aggregate Ethnoreligion label for this source record. It is retained as aggregate context and is not generalized into a statement about every Aizo person's beliefs or practices.

claims.text: The live PeopleGroups.org record PG012297 reports PEID 12297, display name Aizo, country Benin and primary language Gbe, Ayizo (ayb).
Glottolog identifies Ayizo Gbe with glottocode ayiz1245 and ISO 639-3 code ayb and lists Benin as its country.

Glottolog identifies Ayizo Gbe as a distinct languoid, while SIL's Gbe-family overview describes a chaining pattern among Gbe varieties and states that no fully satisfying single dialect-versus-language classification has been established.
claims.interpretationNote: The candidate preserves this classification uncertainty instead of turning one taxonomy into a universal statement about speaker identity.

claims.text: A 2006 Journal of African Languages and Linguistics study documents the tonology of the Ayizo variety of Allada in southern Benin.
claims.interpretationNote: The study is specific to the Allada variety and is not generalized to every Ayizo-speaking locality.

claims.text: The live PeopleGroups.org record reports Ethnoreligion as the aggregate primary-religion label for PG012297.
claims.interpretationNote: This is a provider classification for one people-group-in-country record, not a statement about every Aizo person's belief or practice.
